explanation: Stanley Morison led the design for The Times of London, which first printed in it in October 1932. Its narrow letters fitted more words into each column.

claims.text: The Times of London commissioned the Times New Roman typeface in 1931.

Stanley Morison led the design of Times New Roman for The Times.
The Times first printed in Times New Roman in October 1932.
Times New Roman's relatively narrow letters let more text fit in a newspaper column.

Commission: In 1931 Morison was also typographical consultant to The Times newspaper from 1929 to 1960; and in 1931, having criticised the paper for the poor quality of its printing, he was commissioned by the newspaper to produce a new, easy-to-read typeface.
